title: Canal Seal Commonwealth
rules: 160 independent citizens belong to ten guilds in one connected rectangular canal basin. Citizen roles are tool assignments that consenting neighbors can exchange.
A shovel user at a lock requests opening while an inspector at the exact separate stand checks that the next lock was closed. Closing wins simultaneous conflicts.
Open locks release water every fourth step. Downstream granaries can flood; closed locks with usable headwater feed mills every sixteenth step.
A rope user on each bank, aligned with the barge x coordinate, must choose the same towing direction. Step alongside the barge before towing again.
Carried seals posted at two reciprocal gates waive a limited number of tolls. They expire after 24 steps or uses are exhausted; otherwise toll coins have explicit payer and payee guilds.
Three timber contributions build a persistent bypass. Timber also repairs locks or active barge hulls; these alternatives compete with immediate transport.
The scene uses original parchment land, blue canals and guild insignia. All runtime, learning, transfer and human play claims remain unknown.
